description: Strategic reservoirs and lakes measured by ICESat-2. core is the open-water box [W,S,E,N] the level is read from; refid is the ATL13 water body id inside it. Entries with product "atl06" are read from ATL06 instead (no water mask): levelWindowM bounds the heights the water surface can take, and despikePerGapDayM, where set, raises the despike allowance for a reservoir whose level moves faster than 0.05 m a day. Built with scripts/backfill-reservoir-levels.mjs.

reservoirs.name: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam reservoir
reservoirs.why: Ethiopia's fill of Africa's largest hydropower dam sets how much Blue Nile water reaches Sudan and Egypt.

reservoirs.name: Lake Nasser (Aswan High Dam)
reservoirs.why: Egypt's main water store; its level is the buffer against upstream filling and drought on the Nile.

reservoirs.name: Merowe reservoir
reservoirs.why: Sudan's largest power source, on the Nile downstream of the GERD and inside an active war zone.

reservoirs.name: Roseires reservoir
reservoirs.why: The first Sudanese dam below the GERD; its operation depends directly on Ethiopian releases.

reservoirs.name: Lake Tana
reservoirs.why: Source lake of the Blue Nile, regulated for hydropower and irrigation in northern Ethiopia.

reservoirs.name: Lake Victoria
reservoirs.why: Africa's largest lake feeds the White Nile through Ugandan dams whose releases follow an agreed curve.

reservoirs.name: Ataturk reservoir
reservoirs.why: Turkey's largest reservoir controls Euphrates flow into Syria and Iraq.

reservoirs.name: Keban reservoir
reservoirs.why: The uppermost large Euphrates dam, storing water that later passes Ataturk into Syria.

reservoirs.name: Ilisu reservoir
reservoirs.why: Turkey's Tigris dam, filled since 2019, reduces and times the flow reaching Iraq.

reservoirs.name: Lake Assad (Tabqa Dam)
reservoirs.why: Syria's largest reservoir and power source, held by changing armed forces since 2013.

reservoirs.name: Tishrin reservoir
reservoirs.why: Front-line Euphrates dam in northern Syria whose level tracks upstream Turkish releases and fighting.

reservoirs.name: Mosul Dam reservoir
reservoirs.why: Iraq's largest dam, structurally fragile, storing the Tigris below Turkey.

reservoirs.name: Lake Qadisiyah (Haditha Dam)
reservoirs.why: Iraq's main Euphrates store, a direct read of how much water crosses from Syria.

reservoirs.name: Lake Tharthar
reservoirs.why: Iraq's off-stream flood and drought reserve between the Tigris and the Euphrates.

reservoirs.name: Dukan reservoir
reservoirs.why: Kurdistan Region's main reservoir on a Tigris tributary that rises in Iran.

reservoirs.name: Darbandikhan reservoir
reservoirs.why: Stores the Sirwan below Iran's dams and diversions and supplies power and irrigation water to eastern Iraq.

reservoirs.name: Karkheh reservoir
reservoirs.why: Iran's largest reservoir by storage, upstream of the Hawizeh marshes shared with Iraq.

reservoirs.name: Lake Urmia
reservoirs.why: A shrinking salt lake whose collapse is a test case for Iranian water policy and dust risk.

reservoirs.name: Toktogul reservoir
reservoirs.why: Central Asia's largest reservoir trades Kyrgyz winter power against Uzbek and Kazakh summer irrigation.

reservoirs.name: Nurek reservoir
reservoirs.why: Tajikistan's main power source on an Amu Darya tributary shared with downstream Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan.

reservoirs.name: Tarbela reservoir
reservoirs.why: Pakistan's largest Indus store; its fill and draw-down set irrigation supply for Punjab and Sindh.

reservoirs.name: Mangla reservoir
reservoirs.why: Stores the Jhelum below Indian-administered Kashmir; flows are covered by the Indus Waters Treaty.

reservoirs.name: Gobind Sagar (Bhakra Dam)
reservoirs.why: North India's main irrigation and power store on an Indus-basin river allocated by treaty.

reservoirs.name: Caspian Sea (central basin)
reservoirs.why: A falling Caspian level threatens ports, shipping lanes and oil infrastructure of five states.

reservoirs.name: Three Gorges reservoir
reservoirs.why: The world's largest power station; its level reflects drought and flood management on the Yangtze.

reservoirs.name: Xiaowan reservoir
reservoirs.why: China's largest Mekong store; its filling cuts dry-season flow into Southeast Asia.

reservoirs.name: Nuozhadu reservoir
reservoirs.why: The largest storage on the Mekong mainstem, last major Chinese dam before Laos and Myanmar.

reservoirs.name: Tonle Sap
reservoirs.why: Cambodia's flood-pulse lake and fishery depends on the Mekong flood that upstream dams alter.

reservoirs.name: Nam Ngum reservoir
reservoirs.why: Laos' first large dam, exporting power to Thailand.

reservoirs.name: Lake Kariba
reservoirs.why: Shared Zambia-Zimbabwe reservoir whose drought low in 2024 cut power to both countries.

reservoirs.name: Cahora Bassa reservoir
reservoirs.why: Mozambique's main power source, exporting to South Africa, below Kariba on the Zambezi.

reservoirs.name: Lake Volta
reservoirs.why: Ghana's Akosombo power depends on it, and its level follows rainfall in Burkina Faso.

reservoirs.name: Kainji reservoir
reservoirs.why: Nigeria's main Niger River hydropower store, fed through Mali and Niger.

reservoirs.name: Lake Chad (southern pool)
reservoirs.why: A shrinking shared lake at the centre of the Boko Haram insurgency and regional food insecurity.

reservoirs.name: Lake Turkana
reservoirs.why: A desert lake fed by the Ethiopian Omo; upstream dams and irrigation threaten its level and fishery.

reservoirs.name: Gibe III reservoir
reservoirs.why: Ethiopia's largest dam on the Omo, which sets how much water reaches Lake Turkana in Kenya.

reservoirs.name: Gatun Lake
reservoirs.why: Supplies the Panama Canal locks; its level sets ship draft limits and daily transit caps.

reservoirs.name: Lake Mead
reservoirs.why: Its level triggers shortage tiers for Arizona, Nevada and Mexico on the Colorado River.

reservoirs.name: Lake Powell
reservoirs.why: Upper Colorado store whose level decides Glen Canyon power output and releases to Lake Mead.

reservoirs.name: Guri reservoir
reservoirs.why: Produces most of Venezuela's electricity; low levels have caused national blackouts.

reservoirs.name: Itaipu reservoir
reservoirs.why: Binational Brazil-Paraguay dam supplying most of Paraguay's and a large share of Brazil's power.

reservoirs.name: Furnas reservoir
reservoirs.why: A key store for Brazil's south-east grid; its draw-down tracks national power-rationing risk.

reservoirs.name: Sobradinho reservoir
reservoirs.why: North-east Brazil's main reservoir, feeding hydropower and the Sao Francisco transfer canals.

reservoirs.name: Kakhovka reservoir (destroyed)
reservoirs.why: Drained when its dam was destroyed in June 2023; it supplied southern Ukraine, Crimea canals and nuclear plant cooling.

reservoirs.name: Kremenchuk reservoir
reservoirs.why: Ukraine's largest Dnipro store, part of a cascade under repeated attack.

reservoirs.name: Dnipro reservoir (DniproHES)
reservoirs.why: Store behind the DniproHES dam, struck in 2024, near the front line.

reservoirs.name: Mingachevir reservoir
reservoirs.why: Azerbaijan's largest reservoir on the Kura, the main river of the South Caucasus.

reservoirs.name: Lake Sevan
reservoirs.why: Armenia's strategic freshwater reserve, drawn on for irrigation and power.

reservoirs.name: Sea of Galilee
reservoirs.why: Israel's natural freshwater reservoir, with red-line levels set by law, on the shared Jordan basin.

reservoirs.name: Dead Sea
reservoirs.why: Falling by about a metre a year as Jordan River inflow is diverted upstream.
